# Preface {.unnumbered}

*A personal field guide to becoming a better salesperson — synthesized from six books, tuned for a founder selling their own product.*

This is a private working book. It exists to make me better at selling, not to be published. I keep it in the repo so I can pull it and read it anywhere.

## The six sources

| # | Book | Author | What I take from it |
|---|------|--------|---------------------|
| 1 | **Fanatical Prospecting** | Jeb Blount | Build pipeline |
| 2 | **SPIN Selling** | Neil Rackham | Run discovery |
| 3 | **The Challenger Sale** | Dixon & Adamson | Create demand through insight |
| 4 | **Influence** | Robert Cialdini | Understand buying psychology |
| 5 | **Let's Get Real or Let's Not Play** | Khalsa & Illig | Sell as a trusted advisor |
| 6 | **Never Split the Difference** | Chris Voss | Close and negotiate |

## How this book is organized

It is synthesized by **sales stage**, not summarized book-by-book. Each stage pulls the right author's ideas into the moment of the deal where they matter:

1. Build the pipeline
2. Run discovery
3. Create demand through insight
4. Understand buying psychology *(a lens running under every stage)*
5. Sell as a trusted advisor
6. Close and negotiate

Read the **cheat sheet** first — it's the whole system on one page, the thing to re-read before a call. Then the **stage chapters** go deep. **Founder-led sales resources** adds material beyond the six, and **the operating cadence** turns all of it into a weekly habit.

## Center of gravity

The posture underneath every stage is **trusted advisor**. I use Challenger-style insight to *create demand*, but the intent is always Khalsa's — *the client's success is the only agenda*. Insight opens eyes; it never manipulates.

## The universal frame

> **Diagnose before you prescribe.**

A doctor who prescribes before diagnosing is committing malpractice. So is a seller who pitches before diagnosing. Everything in this book is a variation on that one idea.
